title.zh: 卷二百二十八 列傳第一百十六 魏學曾 李化龍
title.en: Volume 228 Biographies 116: Wei Xueceng, Li Hualong
title.raw: 卷二百二十八 列傳第一百十六 魏學曾 李化龍 Volume 228 Biographies 116: Wei Xueceng, Li Hualong

sentences.zh: 魏學曾

translations.literal: Wei Xueceng
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xueceng

sentences.zh: （葉夢熊梅國楨）〉

translations.literal: (Ye Mengxiong, Mei Guozhen)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (see also: Ye Mengxiong, Mei Guozhen)]〉

sentences.zh: 李化龍

translations.literal: Li Hualong
translations.idiomatic: Li Hualong

sentences.zh: （江鐸）〉

translations.literal: (Jiang Duo)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (see also: Jiang Duo)]〉

sentences.zh: 魏學曾，字惟貫，涇陽人。

translations.literal: Wei Xueceng, style Weiguan, was a native of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xueceng, whose style was Weiguan, came from Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Jiajing 32 (1553).

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事，遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and was later promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and later rose to director.

sentences.zh: 中官為商人請支芻糧銀巨萬，學曾持不可，乃已。

translations.literal: A eunuch requested on behalf of merchants the disbursement of tens of thousands of taels in fodder-grain silver; Xueceng held that it could not be done, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch sought tens of thousands of taels in fodder-grain silver for merchants, Xueceng refused to approve it, and the request was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 尋擢光祿少卿，進右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, advanced to right assistant censor-in-chief, and made grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，土蠻大入永平。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, the Tumen Mongols made a major incursion into Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign, the Tumen Mongols launched a major raid into Yongping.

sentences.zh: 學曾入駐山海，檄諸將王治道等追擊至義院口，大捷。

translations.literal: Xueceng entered and garrisoned Shanhai, ordered the generals Wang Zhidao and others to pursue in attack as far as Yiyuankou, and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng took up headquarters at Shanhai Pass and ordered Wang Zhidao and other generals to pursue the enemy to Yiyuankou, where they won a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 學曾乃易置將吏，招納降附，厘屯田二千余頃，數破敵，被賞賚。

translations.literal: Xueceng then replaced officers and officials, received surrenders and attachments, put in order more than two thousand qing of garrison farmland, repeatedly defeated the enemy, and was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He then reorganized the command staff, accepted defectors, restored more than two thousand qing of garrison farmland, won repeated victories over the enemy, and received imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 以疾去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 起兵部右侍郎，提督神樞營。

translations.literal: He was raised to right vice minister of the Ministry of War and put in charge of the Divine Pivot Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right vice minister of War and placed in command of the Divine Pivot Battalion.

sentences.zh: 旋改吏部，轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 穆宗崩，大學士高拱欲去馮保，屬言官論劾。

translations.literal: When the Muzong emperor died, the grand secretary Gao Gong wished to remove Feng Bao and entrusted censorial officials to memorialize in accusation.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong died, Grand Secretary Gao Gong sought to remove the eunuch Feng Bao and had supervising censors lodge accusations against him.

sentences.zh: 學曾遺書大學士張居正曰：「外人皆言公與保有謀，遺詔亦出公手。

translations.literal: Xueceng sent a letter to the grand secretary Zhang Juzheng, saying: Outsiders all say that you plotted with Bao, and that the testamentary edict also came from your hand.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng wrote to Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng: "People outside court all say you plotted with Feng Bao and that the testamentary edict came from your hand.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，不宜復護此閹。」

translations.literal: In today's affair, it is not fitting again to shield this castrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the present matter you ought not to shield this eunuch again."

sentences.zh: 居正怒。

translations.literal: Juzheng was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was furious.

sentences.zh: 及拱被逐，舉朝失色，學曾獨大言曰：「上踐阼伊始，輒逐顧命大臣，且詔出何人，不可不明示百官。」

translations.literal: When Gong was driven out, the whole court turned pale; Xueceng alone spoke loudly, saying: The sovereign has just ascended the throne and already drives out a entrusted-with-the-regency minister; moreover, from whom did the edict issue—it cannot but be made clear to all officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong was expelled, the whole court was dismayed, but Xueceng alone declared aloud: "The emperor has only just begun his reign and already expels a regent minister; and from whose hand did the edict come? That must be made plain to the entire bureaucracy."

sentences.zh: 要諸大臣詣居正邸爭之。

translations.literal: He demanded that the grand ministers go to Juzheng's residence to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the chief ministers to go to Juzheng's residence and protest.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣多不往，居正亦辭以疾。

translations.literal: Most of the grand ministers did not go; Juzheng also declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers refused to go, and Juzheng himself pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 自是益忤。

translations.literal: From this he became still more at odds.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was increasingly at odds with Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 出為南京右都御史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred out to serve as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 未上，給事中宗弘暹希居正指劾之。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, the supervising secretary Zong Hongxian, hoping to please Juzheng, impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Supervising Secretary Zong Hongxian impeached him at Juzheng's prompting.

sentences.zh: 詔以故官候調，學曾遂歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to await reassignment in his former rank; Xueceng then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left him at his former rank awaiting reassignment, and Xueceng retired home.

sentences.zh: 居正歿逾年，起南京戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: More than a year after Juzheng's death, he was raised to right vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year after Juzheng died, he was recalled as right vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 召為右都御史，督倉場。

translations.literal: He was summoned as right censor-in-chief to supervise the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to Beijing as right censor-in-chief to supervise the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 尋以南京戶部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he retired as minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired with the title of minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十八年，順義王扯撦力克西赴青海，火落赤、真相犯洮河，副總兵李奎、李聯芳先後被殺。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Wanli, the Shunyi prince Chakdak went west to Qinghai; Huoluochi and Zhenxiang invaded the Tao River region, and the vice commanders Li Kui and Li Lianfang were killed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 18 (1590), the Shunyi prince Chakdak moved west into Qinghai while Huoluochi and Zhenxiang raided the Tao River frontier; Vice Commanders Li Kui and Li Lianfang were killed in turn.

sentences.zh: 朝命尚書鄭洛經略七鎮，兼領總督，洛固辭總督。

translations.literal: The court ordered the minister Zheng Luo to take charge of strategy for the seven garrisons and concurrently to hold the post of supreme commander; Luo firmly declined the supreme command.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Minister Zheng Luo to oversee strategy for the seven border garrisons and offered him the supreme command as well, but Luo firmly declined the latter post.

sentences.zh: 明年春，閣臣王錫爵薦學曾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year, the grand secretary Wang Xijue recommended Xueceng.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, Grand Secretary Wang Xijue recommended Xueceng.

sentences.zh: 起兵部尚書，總督陜西、延、寧、甘肅軍務。

translations.literal: He was raised to minister of the Ministry of War and made supreme commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Yan'an, Ningxia, and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of War and supreme commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Yan'an, Ningxia, and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 時洛專主款，學曾至，與議不合，陜西巡撫葉夢熊助之。

translations.literal: At the time Luo devoted himself solely to appeasement; when Xueceng arrived, their counsels did not agree, and the Shaanxi grand coordinator Ye Mengxiong supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo at the time favored appeasement alone; when Xueceng arrived they clashed in counsel, and Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Ye Mengxiong backed Xueceng.

sentences.zh: 初，順義王封，夢熊以諫沮坐得罪，學曾亦為高拱言不便。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shunyi prince was enfeoffed, Mengxiong was punished for remonstrating and obstructing it; Xueceng had also spoken to Gao Gong that it was inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Shunyi title was granted, Mengxiong had been punished for opposing it by remonstrance, and Xueceng too had told Gao Gong that the enfeoffment was ill advised.

sentences.zh: 至是，撦力克助叛，學曾、夢熊欲遂討之，詆洛玩寇。

translations.literal: At this point Chakdak aided the rebels; Xueceng and Mengxiong wished to proceed at once to attack him and denounced Luo for indulging the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Chakdak was aiding the rebels, Xueceng and Mengxiong wanted to attack him immediately and accused Luo of coddling the enemy.

sentences.zh: 會撦力克東歸，火落赤諸部亦徙去，學曾奏撦力克雖歸，陰留精兵二萬於嘉峪，欲助火落赤、真相。

translations.literal: It happened that Chakdak returned east and the various tribes of Huoluochi also moved away; Xueceng memorialized that although Chakdak had returned, he secretly left twenty thousand picked troops at Jiayu and intended to aid Huoluochi and Zhenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chakdak then returned east and Huoluochi's followers also withdrew, but Xueceng reported that although Chakdak had gone back, he had secretly left twenty thousand elite troops at Jiayu Pass to support Huoluochi and Zhenxiang.

sentences.zh: 其說本采諸道路，朝士乃爭附和之。

translations.literal: This account was originally taken from hearsay on the roads, and court gentlemen then vied to echo it.
translations.idiomatic: The story had come from roadside rumor, and court officials soon rushed to endorse it.

sentences.zh: 錫爵意悔，具疏言狀，又遺書責夢熊。

translations.literal: Xijue regretted it in mind, set forth the facts in a memorial, and also sent a letter reproaching Mengxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue had second thoughts, submitted a detailed memorial on the matter, and also wrote to rebuke Mengxiong.

sentences.zh: 而兵部尚書石星以順義既東，宣、大事急，召洛還定撫議，置學曾疏不問。

translations.literal: But the minister of the Ministry of War Shi Xing, because the Shunyi prince had already gone east and the Xuan and Da regions were urgently imperiled, recalled Luo to settle pacification policy and set Xueceng's memorial aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Shi Xing, however, judged that with the Shunyi prince back in the east the Xuan and Da frontier was the urgent concern; he recalled Luo to settle pacification policy and ignored Xueceng's memorial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，河套部長土昧明安入市畢，要請增賞。

translations.literal: Before long, Tumote chief Tümed Ming'an, having finished trading at the market, demanded increased rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Tumote chief Tümed Ming'an, after finishing trade at the border market, demanded larger rewards.

sentences.zh: 學曾令總兵官杜桐、神木參將張剛、孤山遊擊李紹祖出不意擊斬明安，俘馘四百八十余級，奪馬畜器械稱是。

translations.literal: Xueceng ordered the commander-in-chief Du Tong, the Shenmu assistant commander Zhang Gang, and the Gushan mobile corps commander Li Shaozu to strike unexpectedly, kill Ming'an, take more than four hundred eighty heads as captives and trophies, and seize horses, livestock, and weapons in corresponding numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng ordered Commander Du Tong, Shenmu Assistant Commander Zhang Gang, and Gushan Mobile Corps Commander Li Shaozu to launch a surprise attack that killed Ming'an; they took more than four hundred eighty heads and seized horses, livestock, and arms in proportion.

sentences.zh: 學曾以功加太子少保。

translations.literal: Xueceng was advanced to junior guardian of the heir apparent for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: For this exploit Xueceng was promoted to junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 而明安子擺言太聲言復仇，號召諸部。

translations.literal: But Ming'an's son Baitai loudly proclaimed revenge and called together the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an's son Baitai, however, loudly vowed revenge and rallied the tribes.

sentences.zh: 明年，哱拜反，遂煽諸部為亂。

translations.literal: The next year Piba rebelled and then incited the various tribes to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Piba rebelled and stirred the tribes into general disorder.

sentences.zh: 拜，西部人也。

translations.literal: Piba was a man of the western tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Piba came from the western tribes.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中得罪其部長，父兄皆見殺，拜跳脫來降，驍勇屢立戰功。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he offended his tribal chief; his father and elder brothers were all killed; Piba escaped by leaping away and came to surrender; brave and fierce, he repeatedly won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he had fallen out with his tribal chief; his father and brothers were killed, but he escaped and surrendered to the Ming, proving himself a fierce fighter who won repeated battle honors.

sentences.zh: 前督撫王崇古、石茂華先後奏加副總兵，遂多畜亡命。

translations.literal: Former supreme commanders Wang Chonggu and Shi Maohua in succession memorialized to add him as vice commander, and he then kept many fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier supreme commanders Wang Chonggu and Shi Maohua had successively recommended him for promotion to vice commander, and he thereafter gathered many outlaws about him.

sentences.zh: 子承恩，拜夢妖物入妻施脅而生，狼形梟啼，性狠戾。

translations.literal: His son Chengen: Piba dreamed that a demonic thing entered his wife Shi and was born by compulsion; wolf-like in form with owl-like cries, by nature fierce and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengen was said to have been born after Piba dreamed that a demon entered his wife Shi; the child was wolflike in appearance, cried like an owl, and was savage by nature.

sentences.zh: 拜老，承恩襲父爵。

translations.literal: When Piba grew old, Chengen inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: As Piba aged, Chengen inherited his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 十九年，洮、河告警，御史周弘禴舉承恩及指揮土文秀、拜義子哱雲等。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, alarm was raised on the Tao and Yellow River frontiers; the censor Zhou Hongyi recommended Chengen and the commanders Tu Wenxiu, Piba's adopted son Piba Yun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 (1591) alarms sounded on the Tao and Yellow River frontiers, and Censor Zhou Hongyi recommended Chengen along with Commanders Tu Wenxiu and Piba's adopted son Piba Yun.

sentences.zh: 巡撫黨馨檄文秀西援，拜謁經略鄭洛，願與子承恩從出師。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Dang Xin ordered Wenxiu west as reinforcement; Piba called on the frontier commissioner Zheng Luo and wished to follow on campaign with his son Chengen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Dang Xin ordered Wenxiu west as reinforcement; Piba visited Commissioner Zheng Luo and offered to campaign with his son Chengen.

sentences.zh: 馨惡其自薦，抑損之，拜以故心怨。

translations.literal: Xin disliked his volunteering himself and belittled him; Piba therefore bore resentment in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xin disliked his self-recommendation and slighted him, and Piba came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 至金城，見諸鎮兵皆出其下。

translations.literal: When he reached Jincheng, he saw that the troops of the various garrisons were all beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: At Jincheng he saw that the garrison troops ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 比賊退，取道塞外還，寇騎遇之皆辟易，遂有輕中外心。

translations.literal: When the bandits had withdrawn, he returned by way outside the passes; enemy horsemen who met him all gave way, and he then had a mind to look lightly on Chinese and foreigners alike.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march by an outer route after the enemy withdrew, raiding horsemen gave way before him, and he began to despise both Ming and tribal forces alike.

sentences.zh: 馨數裁拜，且按承恩罪箠之二十，雲、文秀亦以他故怨馨。

translations.literal: Xin repeatedly curbed Piba, and moreover prosecuted Chengen for an offense and flogged him twenty strokes; Yun and Wenxiu also resented Xin for other reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Xin repeatedly restrained Piba, prosecuted Chengen for an offense, and had him flogged twenty strokes; Yun and Wenxiu also bore grudges against Xin for other reasons.

sentences.zh: 會戍卒請衣糧久弗給，拜遂嗾軍鋒劉東旸、許朝作亂。

translations.literal: It happened that garrison soldiers had long requested clothing and grain rations without receiving them; Piba then incited the army vanguard Liu Dongyang and Xu Chao to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When long-delayed requests for clothing and rations went unanswered, Piba incited the army vanguards Liu Dongyang and Xu Chao to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，殺馨及副使石繼芳，逼總兵官張維忠縊死。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, they killed Xin and the vice commissioner Shi Jifang and forced the commander-in-chief Zhang Weizhong to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 20 (1592) they killed Dang Xin and Vice Commissioner Shi Jifang and drove Commander Zhang Weizhong to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 雲、文秀殺遊擊梁琦、守備馬承光，東旸稱總兵，奉拜為謀主，承恩、朝為左、右副總兵，雲、文秀為左、右參將。

translations.literal: Yun and Wenxiu killed the mobile corps commander Liang Qi and the garrison commander Ma Chengguang; Dongyang styled himself commander-in-chief, made Piba the chief strategist, made Chengen and Chao left and right vice commanders, and made Yun and Wenxiu left and right assistant commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Wenxiu killed Mobile Corps Commander Liang Qi and Garrison Commander Ma Chengguang; Dongyang proclaimed himself commander-in-chief, made Piba chief strategist, appointed Chengen and Chao left and right vice commanders, and Yun and Wenxiu left and right assistant commanders.

sentences.zh: 承恩遂陷玉泉營、中衛、廣武，河西望風靡。

translations.literal: Chengen then captured Yuchuan Camp, Zhongwei, and Guangwu; west of the river all submitted at the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen then seized Yuchuan Camp, Zhongwei, and Guangwu, and the whole Hexi region collapsed before the rebels.

sentences.zh: 惟文秀徇平虜，參將蕭如薰堅守不下。

translations.literal: Only Wenxiu attacked Pinglu; the assistant commander Xiao Ruxun held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wenxiu besieged Pinglu, where Assistant Commander Xiao Ruxun held out and could not be dislodged.

sentences.zh: 賊既取河西四十七堡，且渡河，復誘河套著力兔、宰僧犯平虜、花馬池。

translations.literal: The bandits, having already taken forty-seven forts west of the river and moreover crossed the river, again enticed the Ordos leaders Zhulitu and Zaiseng to invade Pinglu and Huamachi.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing forty-seven Hexi forts and crossing the river, the rebels induced the Ordos leaders Zhulitu and Zaiseng to attack Pinglu and Huamachi.

sentences.zh: 全陜皆震動。

translations.literal: The whole of Shaanxi was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: All Shaanxi was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 學曾檄副總兵李句率遊擊吳顯趨靈州，別遣遊擊趙武趨鳴沙州，沿河扼賊南渡，而自駐花馬池，當賊衛。

translations.literal: Xueceng ordered the vice commander Li Gou to lead the mobile corps commander Wu Xian in haste to Lingzhou, separately sent the mobile corps commander Zhao Wu in haste to Mingsha Prefecture, along the river to block the bandits' crossing south, and himself garrisoned Huamachi to meet the bandits' assault.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng ordered Vice Commander Li Gou and Mobile Corps Commander Wu Xian to rush to Lingzhou, sent Zhao Wu to Mingsha to block a southern crossing along the river, and himself held Huamachi to face the rebel advance.

sentences.zh: 句等渡河，賊將多遁去，四十七堡皆復，惟寧夏鎮城尚為賊據。

translations.literal: Gou and others crossed the river; most of the bandit generals fled away; all forty-seven forts were recovered; only the Ningxia garrison town was still held by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gou crossed the river, most rebel commanders fled, and all forty-seven forts were recovered, though the Ningxia garrison city remained in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 著力兔等中外相呼應，拜、文秀攻趙武於玉泉。

translations.literal: Zhulitu and others coordinated inside and outside; Piba and Wenxiu attacked Zhao Wu at Yuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhulitu coordinated with the rebels inside and out while Piba and Wenxiu attacked Zhao Wu at Yuchuan.

sentences.zh: 雲引著力兔攻平虜，如薰設伏射殺雲。

translations.literal: Yun led Zhulitu to attack Pinglu; Ruxun set an ambush and shot Yun dead.
translations.idiomatic: Yun led Zhulitu against Pinglu, but Ruxun ambushed and killed Yun.

sentences.zh: 句救武，圍亦解。

translations.literal: Gou rescued Wu and the siege was also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Gou relieved Zhao Wu and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 四月，句引兵與故總兵牛秉忠抵鎮城下。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Gou led troops with the former commander Niu Bingzhong to reach below the garrison town.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Gou advanced with former Commander Niu Bingzhong to the walls of the garrison city.

sentences.zh: 帝已擢董一奎為總兵，李蕡副之，已，復擢如薰代一奎，而以麻貴代蕡。

translations.literal: The emperor had already promoted Dong Yikui as commander-in-chief with Li Fen as his deputy; afterward he again promoted Ruxun to replace Yikui and made Ma Gui replace Fen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had appointed Dong Yikui commander with Li Fen as deputy, then replaced Yikui with Ruxun and Fen with Ma Gui.

sentences.zh: 未至，句等攻城。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Gou and others assaulted the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before the new commanders arrived, Gou and his forces attacked the city.

sentences.zh: 賊於東西二門各出驍騎三千搏戰，步卒列火車為營。

translations.literal: The bandits at the eastern and western gates each sent out three thousand picked horsemen to fight in close combat; foot soldiers arrayed gun carriages as a camp.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent three thousand elite horsemen from each of the east and west gates while infantry formed camps behind gun carriages.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊之，奪其車百輛，追奔入湖，賊溺死無算。

translations.literal: The government army struck them, seized a hundred of their carriages, pursued the fleeing into a lake, and countless bandits drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops routed them, captured a hundred gun carriages, pursued the fugitives into a lake, and drowned countless rebels.

sentences.zh: 副總兵王通戰尤力。

translations.literal: The vice commander Wang Tong fought with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Wang Tong fought with particular vigor.

sentences.zh: 家丁高益等乘勝入北門，後兵不繼被殺，通亦負傷，榆林遊擊俞尚德戰死。

translations.literal: The household retainers Gao Yi and others, riding the victory, entered the north gate; the following troops did not continue and were killed; Tong was also wounded; the Yulin mobile corps commander Yu Shangde died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Household retainers led by Gao Yi broke into the north gate in the pursuit, but unsupported follow-up troops were cut down; Tong was wounded and Yulin Mobile Corps Commander Yu Shangde was killed.

sentences.zh: 翼日，朝、文秀脅慶王上東城，乞暫罷兵，詭言願獻首惡。

translations.literal: The next day, Chao and Wenxiu coerced the Prince of Qing to ascend the east wall, begged a temporary halt to fighting, and falsely claimed willingness to present the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chao and Wenxiu forced the Prince of Qing onto the east wall to plead for a truce, falsely offering to hand over the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 會官軍糧盡，乃引退，休近堡。

translations.literal: It happened that the government army's grain was exhausted; they then withdrew and rested near the forts.
translations.idiomatic: When government provisions ran out, the army withdrew and encamped near the border forts.

sentences.zh: 學曾日夜趣芻餉，調延綏、莊浪、蘭、靖、榆林兵。

translations.literal: Xueceng day and night pressed fodder and supplies and mobilized troops from Yan'an-Suiyuan, Zhuanglang, Lanzhou, Jingzhou, and Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng pressed night and day for fodder and supplies and called up troops from Yan'an-Suiyuan, Zhuanglang, Lanzhou, Jing, and Yulin.

sentences.zh: 道回遠，所治舟亦未具，乃駐花馬池，俟軍至移靈州。

translations.literal: The roads were long in returning, and the boats he was having built were not yet ready; he therefore garrisoned Huamachi and waited for the armies to arrive before moving to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Supply routes were long and his transport boats were not ready, so he remained at Huamachi until the reinforcements arrived before shifting to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，延綏遊擊姜顯謨、都司蕭如蕙，甘州故總兵張傑及麻貴軍皆至，復抵鎮城攻之。

translations.literal: Shortly, the Yan'an-Suiyuan mobile corps commander Jiang Xianmo, the regional commander Xiao Ruhui, the former Gansu commander Zhang Jie, and Ma Gui's army all arrived; they again reached the garrison town and attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiang Xianmo of Yan'an-Suiyuan, Regional Commander Xiao Ruhui, former Gansu Commander Zhang Jie, and Ma Gui's force arrived, and the army again assaulted the garrison city.

sentences.zh: 賊計延綏、榆林兵出內虛，勾黃臺吉妻，令其子舍達大、從子火落赤、土昧鐵雷掠舊安邊、磚井堡以牽我兵。

translations.literal: The bandits calculated that with Yan'an-Suiyuan and Yulin troops out, the interior was empty; they enticed the wife of the Yellow Taiji, ordered her son Sheda, her nephew Huoluochi, and Tümed Tierui to plunder old Anbian and Zhuanjing forts to draw off our troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels judged the interior weak once Yan'an-Suiyuan and Yulin troops had marched out; they enlisted the Yellow Taiji's wife and sent her son Sheda, her nephew Huoluochi, and Tümed Tierui to raid Anbian and Zhuanjing and pin down Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 承恩復以間合寇兵，伏延漢渠，掠糧車二百。

translations.literal: Chengen again joined with enemy troops by secret contact, ambushed at the Yan-Han Canal, and plundered two hundred grain carts.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen again coordinated with outside raiders, ambushed a convoy at the Yan-Han Canal, and seized two hundred grain wagons.

sentences.zh: 學曾自花馬池還靈州，被圍，救至而解。

translations.literal: Xueceng returned from Huamachi to Lingzhou, was surrounded, and was relieved when rescue arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Huamachi to Lingzhou, Xueceng was besieged until relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 貴等數攻城不能克，賊殺慶王妃，盡掠其宮人金帛。

translations.literal: Gui and others repeatedly assaulted the city but could not take it; the bandits killed the consort of the Prince of Qing and plundered all the palace women's gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui and others attacked repeatedly without success; the rebels killed the Prince of Qing's consort and looted the palace women's gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 牛秉忠戰傷右股，乃復退師。

translations.literal: Niu Bingzhong was wounded in battle in the right thigh; the army then withdrew again.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Bingzhong was wounded in the right thigh and the army withdrew once more.

sentences.zh: 帝用尚書星言，賜學曾尚方劍督戰。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Minister Xing's words and bestowed on Xueceng the imperial sword to supervise battle.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on Minister Shi's advice, the emperor granted Xueceng the imperial sword to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 會寧夏巡撫朱正色、甘肅巡撫葉夢熊、監軍御史梅國楨，諸大將劉承嗣、董一奎、李如松先後至軍，六月復攻城，連戰不下。

translations.literal: There gathered the Ningxia grand coordinator Zhu Zhengse, the Gansu grand coordinator Ye Mengxiong, the supervising army censor Mei Guozhen, and the great generals Liu Chengsi, Dong Yikui, and Li Rusong, who in succession reached the army; in the sixth month they again assaulted the city, but after repeated battles could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia Grand Coordinator Zhu Zhengse, Gansu Grand Coordinator Ye Mengxiong, Supervising Censor Mei Guozhen, and generals Liu Chengsi, Dong Yikui, and Li Rusong then joined the campaign; in the sixth month they assaulted the city again but still could not capture it after repeated battles.

sentences.zh: 夢熊，字男兆，歸善人。

translations.literal: Mengxiong, style Nanzhao, was a native of Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong, whose style was Nanzhao, came from Guishan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十年進士。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Jiajing 40 (1561).

sentences.zh: 由福清知縣入為戶部主事，轉餉寧夏。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Fuqing he entered service as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred to supply Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as magistrate of Fuqing he entered the Ministry of Revenue and was assigned to supply the Ningxia front.

sentences.zh: 改御史，以諫受把漢那吉降，貶鄖陽丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to censor; for remonstrating against accepting the surrender of Altan Khan's grandson, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the censorate, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Yunyang for opposing acceptance of Altan Khan's grandson's surrender.

sentences.zh: 累遷贛州知府，平黃鄉賊。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Ganzhou and pacified the Huangxiang bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to prefect of Ganzhou, where he pacified the Huangxiang rebels.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江副使，改永平。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhejiang and then changed to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice commissioner of Zhejiang and was later transferred to Yongping.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年冬，由山東布政使擢右僉都御史，巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventeenth year of Wanli, from Shandong administrative commissioner he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 17 (1589) he was promoted from Shandong administrative commissioner to right assistant censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋改陜西，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Shaanxi and advanced to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Shaanxi and promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 以請討撦力克，與經略洛議相左。

translations.literal: For requesting to attack Chakdak, his counsel opposed that of the frontier commissioner Luo.
translations.idiomatic: His call to attack Chakdak put him at odds with Commissioner Zheng Luo.

sentences.zh: 廷議方右洛，絀其議不用。

translations.literal: Court deliberation at the time favored Luo; his proposal was set aside and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion favored Luo, and Mengxiong's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 會撦力克東歸，洛亦還宣、大，乃移夢熊甘肅，與學曾共事。

translations.literal: It happened that Chakdak returned east and Luo also returned to Xuan and Da; Mengxiong was then transferred to Gansu to work together with Xueceng.
translations.idiomatic: When Chakdak withdrew east and Luo returned to the Xuan and Da frontier, Mengxiong was transferred to Gansu to serve alongside Xueceng.

sentences.zh: 夢熊有膽決，敢任事。

translations.literal: Mengxiong had daring resolution and dared to undertake affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong was bold and decisive and willing to take responsibility.

sentences.zh: 會拜反，上疏自請討賊，帝然之。

translations.literal: When Piba rebelled, he memorialized requesting himself to attack the bandits; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Piba rebelled he volunteered to lead the campaign, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 以六月至靈州，與學曾合。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he reached Lingzhou and joined with Xueceng.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Lingzhou in the sixth month and joined Xueceng's command.

sentences.zh: 國楨，字克生，麻城人。

translations.literal: Guozhen, style Kesheng, was a native of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen, whose style was Kesheng, came from Macheng.

sentences.zh: 少雄傑自喜，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he was heroic and self-pleased, skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was spirited and self-confident, and excelled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he was presented as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 11 (1583).

sentences.zh: 除固安知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Guo'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Guo'an.

sentences.zh: 中官詣國楨請收責於民，國楨偽令民鬻妻以償。

translations.literal: A eunuch came to Guozhen requesting to collect debts from the people; Guozhen falsely ordered the people to sell their wives to pay.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch came to collect debts from the people, Guozhen pretended to order them to sell their wives to pay.

sentences.zh: 民夫婦哀慟，中官為毀券。

translations.literal: The husband and wife grieved and wailed; the eunuch destroyed the bond for them.
translations.idiomatic: The couple wept in distress until the eunuch tore up the bond.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，會拜反，學曾師久無功。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor; when Piba rebelled, Xueceng's army had long been without success.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he found Xueceng's army still bogged down when Piba rebelled.

sentences.zh: 時寧遠伯李成梁方被論，廷議欲遣為大將，未敢決，國楨獨疏保之。

translations.literal: At the time the Earl of Ningyuan Li Chengliang was just being criticized; court deliberation wished to send him as great general but did not dare decide; Guozhen alone memorialized to vouch for him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengliang, Earl of Ningyuan, was then under attack at court; officials wanted him as supreme commander but hesitated, until Guozhen alone memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 乃遣成梁子如松為提督，將遼東、宣、大、山西諸鎮兵以往。

translations.literal: They then sent Chengliang's son Rusong as commissioner-in-chief, leading troops from the Liaodong, Xuan, Da, and Shanxi garrisons thither.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Chengliang's son Li Rusong as commissioner-in-chief at the head of troops from Liaodong, Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 而國楨監其軍，遂與如松至寧夏。

translations.literal: Guozhen supervised his army and thus reached Ningxia with Rusong.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen supervised the army and accompanied Rusong to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 初，學曾欲招東旸、朝，令殺拜父子贖罪，遣卒葉得新往。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xueceng wished to win over Dongyang and Chao, ordering them to kill the Piba father and son to redeem guilt, and sent the soldier Ye Dexin to go.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xueceng had tried to win over Dongyang and Chao by promising pardon if they killed Piba and his son, and sent the soldier Ye Dexin as envoy.

sentences.zh: 四人方約同死，折得新脛，置之獄。

translations.literal: The four men had just agreed to die together; they broke Dexin's shins and put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The four rebels had just sworn to die together; they broke Dexin's legs and threw him in prison.

sentences.zh: 巡撫朱正色以賊詭請降，而張傑嘗總寧夏兵，故與拜善，遣傑入城招之。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Zhu Zhengse, because the bandits falsely requested surrender, and because Zhang Jie had once commanded Ningxia troops and was therefore on good terms with Piba, sent Jie into the city to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhu Zhengse, believing the rebels' false offer of surrender and knowing that former Ningxia commander Zhang Jie was on good terms with Piba, sent Jie into the city to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 朝乃舁得新見傑，得新大罵賊，被殺，傑亦系不遣。

translations.literal: Chao then had Dexin carried in to see Jie; Dexin cursed the bandits loudly and was killed; Jie was also detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Chao had Dexin brought before Jie; Dexin cursed the rebels and was killed, and Jie was detained as well.

sentences.zh: 而學曾以賊求撫為之請，帝切責。

translations.literal: Moreover Xueceng petitioned on the bandits' request for pacification; the emperor sternly reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueceng petitioned on behalf of the rebels' request for pacification, the emperor rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 及是，城中百戶姚欽、武生張遐齡射書城外，約內應，夜半舉火。

translations.literal: At this point, the hundred-household head Yao Qin and the military licentiate Zhang Xialing shot a letter outside the wall, arranging an inside response; at midnight they raised fire.
translations.idiomatic: By then the hundred-household head Yao Qin and military licentiate Zhang Xialing shot messages over the wall arranging a rising within; at midnight they lit signal fires.

sentences.zh: 外兵不至，賊殺其黨五十人，欽縋城出，來奔。

translations.literal: The outside troops did not arrive; the bandits killed fifty of their own party; Qin was lowered by rope from the wall and came to flee to the government side.
translations.idiomatic: When outside troops failed to come, the rebels executed fifty of their own men; Qin was lowered from the wall by rope and fled to the Ming camp.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊外以求撫緩兵，而陰結寇為助，然糧盡，勢且困。

translations.literal: At this time, outwardly the bandits sought pacification to slow the army, while secretly they joined with raiders for aid; yet grain was exhausted and their situation was about to be desperate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels outwardly sought pacification to gain time while secretly enlisting outside raiders, but their grain was exhausted and they were nearing collapse.

sentences.zh: 七月，學曾與夢熊、國楨定計，決黃河大壩水灌之，水抵城下。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Xueceng with Mengxiong and Guozhen fixed a plan, breached the Yellow River great dam to flood them, and the water reached below the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xueceng, Mengxiong, and Guozhen decided to breach the Yellow River dam and flood the city; the water reached the walls.

sentences.zh: 時套寇卜失兔、莊禿賴以三萬騎犯定邊、小鹽池，用土昧鐵雷為前鋒，而別遣宰僧以萬騎從花馬池西沙湃口入，為拜聲援。

translations.literal: At the time the Ordos raiders Bushitu and Zhuangtulai with thirty thousand horsemen invaded Dingbian and Xiaoyanchi, using Tümed Tierui as vanguard, while separately sending Zaiseng with ten thousand horsemen to enter from the Shapai Pass west of Huamachi as reinforcement for Piba.
translations.idiomatic: Ordos leaders Bushitu and Zhuangtulai then struck Dingbian and Xiaoyanchi with thirty thousand horsemen, Tierui in the van, while Zaiseng led ten thousand horsemen through Shapai Pass west of Huamachi to support Piba.

sentences.zh: 麻貴擊之右溝，寇稍挫，分趨下馬關及鳴沙洲。

translations.literal: Ma Gui struck them at Yougou; the raiders were slightly checked and split toward Xiamaguan and Mingshazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gui met them at Yougou, checked the raid, and drove the raiders toward Xiamaguan and Mingshazhou.

sentences.zh: 學曾令遊擊龔子敬扼沙湃口，而檄延綏總兵官董一元搗土昧鐵雷巢，斬首百三十余級，寇大驚引去。

translations.literal: Xueceng ordered the mobile corps commander Gong Zijing to hold Shapai Pass and sent orders to the Yan'an-Suiyuan commander Dong Yiyuan to strike Tümed Tierui's nest, beheading more than one hundred thirty; the raiders were greatly alarmed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng ordered Gong Zijing to hold Shapai Pass and directed Yan'an-Suiyuan Commander Dong Yiyuan to raid Tierui's camp, taking more than one hundred thirty heads and sending the raiders fleeing in alarm.

sentences.zh: 遇子敬，圍之十重，子敬死，寇亦去，賊援遂絕。

translations.literal: They met Zijing, surrounded him ten layers deep; Zijing died; the raiders also left; the bandits' reinforcements were thus cut off.
translations.idiomatic: They then surrounded Zijing ten ranks deep and killed him before withdrawing, and the rebels' outside support was cut off.

sentences.zh: 學曾益決大壩水。

translations.literal: Xueceng further breached the great dam water.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng then increased the flow from the breached dam.

sentences.zh: 八月，河決堤壞，復繕治之，城外水深八九尺，東西城崩百余丈。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the river burst the dike and it was ruined; they repaired it again; outside the city the water was eight or nine chi deep; the eastern and western walls collapsed for more than a hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the dike burst and had to be repaired again; water outside the walls stood eight or nine feet deep, and more than a hundred zhang of the east and west walls collapsed.

sentences.zh: 著力兔、宰僧復入李剛堡。

translations.literal: Zhulitu and Zaiseng again entered Ligang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhulitu and Zaiseng again entered Ligang Fort.

sentences.zh: 如松、貴等擊敗之，追奔至賀蘭山。

translations.literal: Rusong, Gui, and others defeated them and pursued the fleeing as far as Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong, Ma Gui, and others routed them and pursued them to Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊益懼求款，未決，會學曾得罪罷。

translations.literal: The bandits grew still more fearful and sought terms; before it was decided, it happened that Xueceng offended and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew desperate and sought terms, but before terms were settled Xueceng was dismissed for his offenses.

sentences.zh: 朝命以夢熊代，夢熊遂成功。

translations.literal: The court ordered Mengxiong to replace him; Mengxiong then achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced him with Mengxiong, who then brought the campaign to success.

sentences.zh: 初，學曾之遣人招東旸、朝也，留固原十余日以俟之，帝責其玩寇；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xueceng sent men to win over Dongyang and Chao, he remained at Guyuan more than ten days to await them; the emperor reproached him for indulging the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xueceng sent envoys to win over Dongyang and Chao, he had waited at Guyuan more than ten days, and the emperor accused him of indulging the enemy;

sentences.zh: 李句渡河又稍遲，松山、河套寇先入，官軍用是再失利。

translations.literal: Li Gou's crossing the river was again somewhat late; Songshan and Ordos raiders entered first; the government army therefore suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gou's river crossing was again delayed, allowing Songshan and Ordos raiders to strike first, and government forces suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 學曾嘗上疏令監軍無與兵事，帝為飭國楨如其言，國楨頗憾之。

translations.literal: Xueceng had once memorialized ordering supervising army officials not to interfere in military affairs; the emperor admonished Guozhen according to his words; Guozhen was quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng had once memorialized that supervising censors should not interfere in military affairs; the emperor ordered Guozhen accordingly, to Guozhen's resentment.

sentences.zh: 及至軍，劾諸將觀望，而頗以玩寇為學曾罪。

translations.literal: When he reached the army, he impeached the generals for watching and waiting, and largely made indulging the enemy Xueceng's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the front he impeached the generals for hesitation and largely blamed Xueceng for indulging the enemy.

sentences.zh: 給事中許子偉亦劾學曾惑於招撫，誤國事。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Xu Ziwei also impeached Xueceng for being deluded by pacification and misleading state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Ziwei also impeached Xueceng for being misled by pacification schemes and harming the state.

sentences.zh: 國楨又言僉事隨府從城上躍下，賊令四人下取，我軍咫尺不敢前；

translations.literal: Guozhen also said that the administrative vice commissioner Suifu leaped down from the wall; the bandits ordered four men down to seize him, and our army within a foot's distance dared not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen also reported that Vice Commissioner Suifu leaped from the wall, that the rebels sent four men down to seize him while Ming troops a few feet away dared not advance;

sentences.zh: 又北寇數萬斷我糧道，殺戮無算，匿不以奏。

translations.literal: Moreover tens of thousands of northern raiders cut our grain route, killing and slaughtering beyond count, which he concealed and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: and that tens of thousands of northern raiders had cut the supply route with countless killings, which Xueceng had concealed from the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝遂大怒，逮學曾至京。

translations.literal: The emperor then was greatly angry and arrested Xueceng to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had Xueceng arrested and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 然學曾逮未逾月，城壞而大軍入，賊竟以破滅。

translations.literal: Yet before Xueceng's arrest had passed a month, the walls were ruined and the great army entered; the bandits were finally destroyed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet less than a month after his arrest the walls collapsed, the main army entered, and the rebels were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 夢熊既代學曾，亦賜尚方劍。

translations.literal: After Mengxiong replaced Xueceng, he too was bestowed the imperial sword.
translations.idiomatic: After replacing Xueceng, Mengxiong too received the imperial sword.

sentences.zh: 時調度靈州，獨國楨監軍寧夏。

translations.literal: At the time he directed affairs from Lingzhou; Guozhen alone supervised the army at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong directed operations from Lingzhou while Guozhen alone supervised the army at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 賊被圍久，食盡無援，而城受水浸，益大崩。

translations.literal: The bandits had long been besieged, food was exhausted and there was no aid, and the city, soaked by water, collapsed still more greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged for months, the rebels had exhausted their food and outside aid while floodwater further undermined the walls.

sentences.zh: 國楨挾諸將趨南關。

translations.literal: Guozhen urged the generals toward the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen drove the generals toward the south gate.

sentences.zh: 秉忠先登，國楨大呼，諸將畢登。

translations.literal: Bingzhong mounted first; Guozhen shouted loudly; all the generals mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong scaled the wall first; Guozhen shouted encouragement, and the other generals followed.

sentences.zh: 賊退據大城，攻數日不下。

translations.literal: The bandits withdrew to hold the great inner city; assaulted for several days, it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to the inner citadel, which resisted assault for several days.

sentences.zh: 國楨使間紿東旸、朝、承恩互相殺，以降貰其罪。

translations.literal: Guozhen used secret agents to deceive Dongyang, Chao, and Chengen into mutual killing, promising that surrender would redeem their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen used agents to deceive Dongyang, Chao, and Chengen into turning on one another, promising pardon if they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三人內猜疑，東旸、朝遂先誘殺承恩黨文秀。

translations.literal: The three men suspected one another inwardly; Dongyang and Chao then first lured and killed Chengen's partisan Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual suspicion set in, and Dongyang and Chao first lured and killed Chengen's follower Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 承恩亦與其黨周國柱誘東旸、朝殺之；

translations.literal: Chengen also with his partisan Zhou Guozhu lured Dongyang and Chao and killed them;
translations.idiomatic: Chengen then joined his follower Zhou Guozhu in luring and killing Dongyang and Chao;

sentences.zh: 盡懸東旸、朝、文秀首城上，開門降。

translations.literal: They hung all the heads of Dongyang, Chao, and Wenxiu on the wall and opened the gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: they hung the heads of Dongyang, Chao, and Wenxiu on the wall and opened the gates in surrender.

sentences.zh: 如松率兵圍拜家。

translations.literal: Rusong led troops to surround Piba's house.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong surrounded Piba's residence.

sentences.zh: 拜倉皇縊，闔室自焚死。

translations.literal: Piba in panic hanged himself; the whole household burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: Piba hanged himself in panic while his entire household burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 夢熊自靈州馳至，下令盡誅拜黨及降人二千，慰問宗室士庶。

translations.literal: Mengxiong galloped from Lingzhou and arrived, ordering the execution of all Piba's party and two thousand who had surrendered, and comforting the imperial clan, scholars, and common people.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong galloped from Lingzhou and ordered the execution of Piba's entire faction and two thousand surrendering rebels, then comforted the imperial clan and local populace.

sentences.zh: 寧夏平。

translations.literal: Ningxia was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia was pacified.

sentences.zh: 夢熊、正色、國楨各上捷奏，而俘承恩獻京師。

translations.literal: Mengxiong, Zhengse, and Guozhen each submitted victory memorials, and the captive Chengen was presented at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong, Zhengse, and Guozhen each reported victory, and Chengen was sent to the capital as a captive.

sentences.zh: 帝御門受賀，詔磔承恩於市，夢熊、正色、國楨各蔭世官，如松功第一，如薰、貴、秉忠等加恩有差。

translations.literal: The emperor received congratulations at the palace gate, ordered Chengen dismembered in the market, granted hereditary offices to Mengxiong, Zhengse, and Guozhen, ranked Rusong's merit first, and increased favors for Ruxun, Gui, Bingzhong, and others with differences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received congratulations at the palace gate, ordered Chengen dismembered in the marketplace, granted hereditary offices to Mengxiong, Zhengse, and Guozhen, ranked Rusong first in merit, and rewarded Ruxun, Ma Gui, Bingzhong, and others in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 學曾初奪職為民，敘功，以原官致仕。

translations.literal: Xueceng at first was stripped of office and made a commoner; when merits were recounted, he retired with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng had first been reduced to commoner status, but when merits were tallied he was allowed to retire with his former rank.

sentences.zh: 學曾任事勞勚。

translations.literal: Xueceng in service toiled with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng had served with exhausting merit.

sentences.zh: 灌城招降之策，本其所建。

translations.literal: The strategy of flooding the city and winning surrender had originally been his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy of flooding the city and inducing surrender had been his plan from the start.

sentences.zh: 及宣捷，帝召見大學士趙誌臯、張位，誌臯、位力為學曾解，尚書星以下多白學曾無罪。

translations.literal: When victory was announced, the emperor summoned the grand secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei; Zhigao and Wei strongly pleaded for Xueceng; Minister Xing and those below mostly declared Xueceng innocent.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was announced, the emperor summoned Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei, who strongly defended Xueceng, while Minister Shi and others declared him innocent.

sentences.zh: 國楨亦上疏言：「學曾應變稍緩，臣請責諸將以振士氣，而逮學曾之命，發自臣疏，竊自悔恨。

translations.literal: Guozhen also memorialized, saying: Xueceng in responding to change was somewhat slow; your servant requested to blame the generals to rouse army morale, yet the order to arrest Xueceng issued from your servant's memorial; I privately regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen also memorialized: "Xueceng was somewhat slow in adapting to events; I asked to blame the generals to restore morale, but the order to arrest him came from my own memorial, for which I deeply regret myself.

sentences.zh: 學曾不早雪，臣將受萬世譏。」

translations.literal: If Xueceng is not cleared early, your servant will receive the scorn of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If Xueceng is not cleared soon, I shall be scorned for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 如松亦言：「學曾被逮時，三軍雨泣。」

translations.literal: Rusong also said: When Xueceng was arrested, the three armies wept like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong added: "When Xueceng was arrested, the whole army wept like rain."

sentences.zh: 夢熊亦推功學曾。

translations.literal: Mengxiong also attributed merit to Xueceng.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong also credited the victory to Xueceng.

sentences.zh: 帝初不聽，既而復其官。

translations.literal: The emperor at first did not listen; afterward he restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first refused, but later restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 居家數年卒。

translations.literal: He dwelt at home several years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home several years and died.

sentences.zh: 夢熊以功進右都御史。

translations.literal: Mengxiong for merit was advanced to right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Mengxiong was promoted to right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，卜失兔為都督，其部長切盡臺吉最用事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bushitu was a commissioner-in-chief; among his tribal chiefs Qiejin Taiji was most influential.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bushitu held the rank of commissioner-in-chief, and among his chiefs Qiejin Taiji had been the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 切盡臺吉死，卜失兔不能制諸部。

translations.literal: When Qiejin Taiji died, Bushitu could not control the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiejin Taiji died, Bushitu could no longer control the tribes.

sentences.zh: 經略鄭洛專事羈縻。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Zheng Luo devoted himself solely to loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Zheng Luo relied entirely on appeasement.

sentences.zh: 學曾以洮河之變，惡諸部為逆，襲殺明安。

translations.literal: Xueceng, because of the Tao River disturbance, hated the tribes as rebels and launched a surprise attack killing Ming'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tao River crisis Xueceng treated the tribes as enemies and launched a surprise attack that killed Ming'an.

sentences.zh: 會拜反，著力兔、宰僧遂聲言與拜為一家，而卜失兔、莊禿賴亦引兵助之。

translations.literal: When Piba rebelled, Zhulitu and Zaiseng then proclaimed themselves of one family with Piba, while Bushitu and Zhuangtulai also led troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Piba rebelled, Zhulitu and Zaiseng declared themselves kin to him, and Bushitu and Zhuangtulai also marched to his aid.

sentences.zh: 及拜誅，切盡臺吉之比吉率著力兔、宰僧、莊禿賴等頓首花馬池塞下，悔罪求款。

translations.literal: When Piba was executed, Qiejin Taiji's nephew Biji led Zhulitu, Zaiseng, Zhuangtulai, and others to kowtow below the pass at Huamachi, repent their crimes, and seek terms.
translations.idiomatic: After Piba's death, Qiejin Taiji's nephew Biji led Zhulitu, Zaiseng, Zhuangtulai, and others to kowtow at Huamachi Pass, repent, and sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 夢熊為奏請。

translations.literal: Mengxiong memorialized requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong memorialized on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝以夢熊初主學曾，責其前後異議，令要諸部縛叛贖罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Mengxiong had at first supported Xueceng, reproached his shifting counsel before and after, and ordered the tribes to bind rebels and redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting Mengxiong's earlier support for Xueceng, rebuked his inconsistency and ordered the tribes to hand over rebels to atone.

sentences.zh: 著力兔等求款益堅，夢熊乃與巡撫田樂奏上四鎮款戰機宜，俟朝議。

translations.literal: Zhulitu and others sought terms ever more firmly; Mengxiong then with the grand coordinator Tian Le memorialized the four garrisons' policy for peace and war, awaiting court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhulitu and others pressed harder for peace, Mengxiong and Grand Coordinator Tian Le submitted a plan for war and peace on the four garrisons and awaited court decision.

sentences.zh: 中外相仗莫敢決，卜失兔遂率諸部大入定邊。

translations.literal: Inside and outside relied on one another and none dared decide; Bushitu then led the tribes in a great invasion of Dingbian.
translations.idiomatic: Court and frontier officials deferred to one another and dared not decide, and Bushitu then led the tribes in a major invasion of Dingbian.

sentences.zh: 總兵官麻貴等擊卻之，夢熊以功加太子少保。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Ma Gui and others struck and repelled them; Mengxiong for merit was advanced to junior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Ma Gui and others drove them back, and Mengxiong was promoted to junior guardian of the heir apparent for the exploit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，切盡臺吉從子青把都兒犯甘肅，總兵官楊浚、副總兵何崇德禦之，斬首六百余級。

translations.literal: Before long, Qiejin Taiji's nephew Qingbadu'er invaded Gansu; the commander-in-chief Yang Jun and vice commander He Chongde defended against him and beheaded more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qiejin Taiji's nephew Qingbadu'er raided Gansu; Commander Yang Jun and Vice Commander He Chongde repelled him and took more than six hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 夢熊復加太子太保、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Mengxiong was again advanced to grand guardian of the heir apparent and minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong was further promoted to grand guardian of the heir apparent and minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋入為南京工部尚書，而以都御史李汶代。

translations.literal: Soon he entered service as minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works, and the censor-in-chief Li Wen replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the capital as minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works, and Censor-in-Chief Li Wen replaced him on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 自洮河變後，寇頗輕中國。

translations.literal: Since the Tao River disturbance, the raiders have rather looked lightly on China.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tao River crisis the raiders came to hold China in less regard.

sentences.zh: 招撫議既絕，諸部數入犯，四鎮遂頻歲用兵雲。

translations.literal: Once pacification talks were ended, the tribes repeatedly invaded, and the four garrisons thus waged war year after year—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: With pacification abandoned, the tribes raided repeatedly, and the four garrisons were at war year after year.

sentences.zh: 夢熊雖功多，其品望遠出學曾下。

translations.literal: Although Mengxiong had many merits, his standing in character was far below Xueceng's.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mengxiong won many victories, his reputation stood far below Xueceng's.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 國楨既招降承恩，以夢熊貪功殺降，劾其罪。

translations.literal: Guozhen, having induced Chengen to surrender, impeached Mengxiong for greed for merit in killing those who had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen, who had induced Chengen to surrender, impeached Mengxiong for slaughtering the surrendered out of greed for credit.

sentences.zh: 夢熊奏辨，言：「拜所畜家人皆死士，緩一二日，東旸、朝黨復集，必再亂。

translations.literal: Mengxiong memorialized in defense, saying: The household retainers Piba kept were all death-fighters; delay a day or two and the Dongyang and Chao factions would gather again and surely rebel once more.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong replied in a memorial: "Piba's retainers were all fanatics; delay a day or two and Dongyang's and Chao's followers would rally again and surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 臣寧負殺降名，以絕禍本。」

translations.literal: Your servant would rather bear the name of killing those who surrendered, to cut off the root of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather bear the name of slaughtering surrendering men than leave the seeds of another revolt."

sentences.zh: 帝為下詔和解之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict to settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 論功，擢國楨太仆少卿。

translations.literal: When merits were discussed, Guozhen was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were rewarded, Guozhen was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遷右僉都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to right assistant censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became right assistant censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷兵部右侍郎，總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to right vice minister of the Ministry of War and made supreme commander of military affairs in Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he became right vice minister of War and supreme commander of military affairs in Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 在鎮三年，節省市賞銀十五萬兩有奇。

translations.literal: During three years at the garrison he economized and saved more than one hundred fifty thousand taels in market reward silver.
translations.idiomatic: In three years on the frontier he saved more than one hundred fifty thousand taels in border reward silver.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸，未起而卒。

translations.literal: He returned on his father's mourning and died before being raised again.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home for his father's mourning and died before being recalled.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 李化龍，字於田，長垣人。

translations.literal: Li Hualong, style Yutian, was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hualong, whose style was Yutian, came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 2 (1574).

sentences.zh: 除嵩縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Song County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Song County.

sentences.zh: 年甫二十，胥吏易之。

translations.literal: He was only twenty years old; the clerks and runners looked lightly on him.
translations.idiomatic: Only twenty years old, he was underestimated by the yamen staff.

sentences.zh: 化龍陰察其奸，悉召置之法，縣中大治。

translations.literal: Hualong secretly investigated their wrongdoing, summoned them all and dealt with them by law; the county was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong secretly investigated their corruption, summoned them all to justice, and brought the county under firm order.

sentences.zh: 遷南京工部主事，歷右通政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and served through as right commissioner of transport.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and later became right commissioner of transport.

sentences.zh: 二十二年夏，擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-second year he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 22 (1594) he was promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 初，總兵官李成梁破殺泰寧速把亥，其子把兔兒弟炒花據舊遼陽以北，居兩河之中，益結土蠻為患。

translations.literal: Earlier, the commander-in-chief Li Chengliang defeated and killed Taining Subahai; his son Batuer and younger brother Chaohua held the region north of old Liaoyang, dwelling between the two rivers, and increasingly joined with the Tumen Mongols to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Commander Li Chengliang had defeated and killed the Taining chief Subahai; his son Batuer and brother Chaohua held the country north of old Liaoyang between the two rivers and increasingly allied with the Tumen Mongols.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，把兔兒圍遼陽，朵顏小歹青、福余伯言兒分犯錦、義，掠清細河，巡撫韓取善坐免。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year Batuer besieged Liaoyang; the Tümed Xiaodaqing and Fuyu Boyan'er separately invaded Jin and Yi, plundered the Qingxi River region, and Grand Coordinator Han Qushan was dismissed for his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: That April Batuer besieged Liaoyang while Xiaodaqing of the Tümed and Boyan'er of Fuyu raided Jinzhou and Yizhou and plundered along the Qingxi River; Grand Coordinator Han Qushan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 化龍受事甫兩月，把兔兒與伯言兒等寇鎮武，又約土蠻子卜言臺周犯右屯。

translations.literal: Hualong had taken office only two months when Batuer with Boyan'er and others raided Zhenwu, and also arranged with the Tumen son Buyantaiju to invade Youdun.
translations.idiomatic: Only two months into office, Hualong faced Batuer and Boyan'er raiding Zhenwu while Buyantaiju of the Tumen was enlisted to strike Youdun.

sentences.zh: 把兔兒先至吳家墳。

translations.literal: Batuer arrived first at Wujiafen.
translations.idiomatic: Batuer reached Wujiafen first.

sentences.zh: 化龍與總兵官董一元定計先擊把兔、伯言兒，伯言兒中流矢死，把兔被傷。

translations.literal: Hualong with the commander-in-chief Dong Yiyuan fixed a plan to strike Batuer and Boyan'er first; Boyan'er was hit by a stray arrow and died; Batuer was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong and Commander Dong Yiyuan decided to strike Batuer and Boyan'er first; Boyan'er was killed by a stray arrow and Batuer was wounded.

sentences.zh: 卜言臺周至，攻右屯不利，亦解去。

translations.literal: Buyantaiju arrived, attacked Youdun without success, and also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Buyantaiju arrived, failed against Youdun, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是把兔、小歹青、卜言臺周益相結，謀復前恥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Batuer, Xiaodaqing, and Buyantaiju increasingly joined together, plotting to recover their former shame.
translations.idiomatic: Batuer, Xiaodaqing, and Buyantaiju then drew closer together, plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 化龍與一元嚴備之。

translations.literal: Hualong and Yiyuan made strict preparations against them.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong and Yiyuan tightened defenses.

sentences.zh: 一元又出塞，搗巢有功，而把兔傷重竟死，邊塞詟服。

translations.literal: Yiyuan again went outside the passes, raided nests with merit, and Batuer, his wounds grave, finally died; the border passes were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan raided beyond the passes with success; Batuer died of his wounds, and the frontier was cowed into submission.

sentences.zh: 詳具一元傳。

translations.literal: Details are fully set forth in the biography of Yiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Dong Yiyuan for full details.

sentences.zh: 化龍進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Hualong was advanced to right vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong was promoted to right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，小歹青悔禍款塞，請開木市於義州，且告朵顏長昂將犯邊。

translations.literal: The next year Xiaodaqing repented the calamity and sought terms at the passes, requesting to open a timber market at Yizhou, and also reported that the Tümed Changang would invade the border.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xiaodaqing repented and sued for peace, asking to open a timber market at Yizhou and warning that the Tümed leader Changang would raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 已，長昂果犯錦、義，副總兵李如梅擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Changang indeed invaded Jin and Yi; the vice commander Li Rumei struck and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Changang soon did raid Jinzhou and Yizhou, but Vice Commander Li Rumei drove him back.

sentences.zh: 歹青言既信，化龍遂許其請。

translations.literal: Since Daqing's words had proved trustworthy, Hualong then granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiaodaqing's warning vindicated, Hualong approved his request.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized as follows:

sentences.zh: 環遼皆敵也，迤北土蠻種類多不可數。

translations.literal: All around Liaodong are enemies; northward the Tumen Mongol kinds are many beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies surround Liaodong on every side, and northward the Tumen tribes are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 近邊者，直寧前則長昂，直錦、義則小歹青，直廣寧、遼、瀋則把兔、炒花、花大，直開、鐵則伯言、暖兔，其在東邊海西則猛骨孛羅、那林孛羅、卜寨，皆與遼地項背相望。

translations.literal: Those near the border: facing Ningqian directly is Changang; facing Jin and Yi is Xiaodaqing; facing Guangning, Liaoyang, and Shenyang are Batuer, Chaohua, and Huada; facing Kaiyuan and Tieling are Boyan and Nuantu; those in the eastern Haixi are Mengguboluo, Nalinboluo, and Bozhai—all back to back with Liaodong territory.
translations.idiomatic: Along the frontier: Changang faces Ningqian; Xiaodaqing faces Jinzhou and Yizhou; Batuer, Chaohua, and Huada face Guangning, Liaoyang, and Shenyang; Boyan and Nuantu face Kaiyuan and Tieling; and the eastern Haixi leaders Mengguboluo, Nalinboluo, and Bozhai all stand back to back with Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 並墻圍獵，則刁鬥聲相聞，蓋肘腋憂也。

translations.literal: Hunting along the same wall, watch-drums are heard one from another—truly a worry in one's armpits.
translations.idiomatic: They hunt along the same border wall within earshot of one another's watch-drums—a constant threat at the armpit.

sentences.zh: 自那卜被剿，數年東陲無事。

translations.literal: Since Napu was suppressed, for several years the eastern frontier was without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Since Napu was crushed, the eastern frontier had been quiet for several years.

sentences.zh: 去年把兔、伯言戰死，炒花、花大一敗塗地。

translations.literal: Last year Batuer and Boyan died in battle; Chaohua and Huada suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Batuer and Boyan were killed in battle and Chaohua and Huada were routed utterly.

sentences.zh: 今伯言子宰賽受罰，入市廣寧，遼、瀋、開、鐵間警報漸希。

translations.literal: Now Boyan's son Zaisai has accepted punishment and entered the market at Guangning; between Liaoyang, Shenyang, Kaiyuan, and Tieling alarms have gradually grown rare.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan's son Zaisai has submitted and trades at Guangning, and alarms between Liaoyang, Shenyang, Kaiyuan, and Tieling have grown rare.

sentences.zh: 所未馴伏者，惟小歹青與長昂耳。

translations.literal: Those not yet tamed and subdued are only Xiaodaqing and Changang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiaodaqing and Changang remain unsubdued.

sentences.zh: 小歹青素兇狡，雄長諸部。

translations.literal: Xiaodaqing by nature is fierce and cunning and dominates the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaodaqing is naturally fierce and cunning and dominates the tribes.

sentences.zh: 西助長昂，東助炒花。

translations.literal: Westward he aids Changang; eastward he aids Chaohua.
translations.idiomatic: He supports Changang in the west and Chaohua in the east.

sentences.zh: 大舉動以數萬，小竊則飛騎出沒錦、義間。

translations.literal: In great campaigns he moves with tens of thousands; in small thefts swift horsemen appear and vanish between Jin and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Major raids number in the tens of thousands; smaller raids send swift horsemen raiding between Jinzhou and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 自周之望、柏朝翠戰歿，無敢以一矢加遺。

translations.literal: Since Zhou Zhiwang and Bai Chaochui died in battle, none has dared add a single arrow against him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou Zhiwang and Bai Chaochui fell in battle, no one has dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 淩河上下方數百里，野多暴骨，民無寧宇。

translations.literal: Up and down the Ling River for several hundred li, the wilds hold many bones of the violently slain; the people have no peaceful dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: For hundreds of li along the Ling River the countryside is strewn with the bones of the slain and the people know no peace.

sentences.zh: 遠慮者每以河西不保為虞。

translations.literal: Those of far-reaching concern often worry that Hexi cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Far-sighted men constantly feared that the region west of the river could not be held.

sentences.zh: 今乃叩關求市，臣遍詢將領及彼地居民，僉言木市開有五利。

translations.literal: Now he knocks at the passes seeking a market; your servant has widely questioned generals and residents of that region, and all say that opening the timber market has five benefits.
translations.idiomatic: Now he seeks entry to trade at the passes; I have questioned generals and local residents, and all agree that opening a timber market would bring five benefits.

sentences.zh: 河西無木，皆在邊外，叛亂以來，仰給河東，以邊警又不時至。

translations.literal: Hexi has no timber; it is all outside the border. Since the rebellions, it has relied on supply from east of the river, yet border alarms also arrive from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi has no timber of its own—all lies beyond the border. Since the rebellions it has depended on the east bank, and border alarms interrupt supply.

sentences.zh: 故河西木貴於玉，市通則材木不可勝用。

translations.literal: Therefore timber in Hexi is dearer than jade; once the market is open, lumber and timber will be more than can be used up.
translations.idiomatic: Timber in Hexi is therefore dearer than jade; once trade opens, lumber will be abundant.

sentences.zh: 利一。

translations.literal: Benefit one.
translations.idiomatic: First benefit.

sentences.zh: 所疑於歹青者，無信耳。

translations.literal: What is doubted about Daqing is only lack of trust.
translations.idiomatic: The only doubt about Xiaodaqing is trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 彼重市為生路，當市時必不行掠。

translations.literal: He values the market as his road to life; during market times he surely will not raid.
translations.idiomatic: He values trade as his livelihood and will not raid during market season.

sentences.zh: 即今年市而明年掠，我已收今年不掠之利矣。

translations.literal: Even if he markets this year and raids next year, we have already gained this year's benefit of no raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he trades this year and raids next, we still gain a year without raids.

sentences.zh: 利二。

translations.literal: Benefit two.
translations.idiomatic: Second benefit.

sentences.zh: 遼東馬市，成祖所開，無他賞，本聽商民與交易。

translations.literal: The Liaodong horse market, opened by the Chengzu emperor, has no other rewards; it originally allowed merchants and common people to trade.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong horse market opened by the Yongle emperor involved no special rewards and simply allowed merchants and civilians to trade.

sentences.zh: 木市與馬市等，有利於民，不費於官。

translations.literal: The timber market is like the horse market—beneficial to the people, not costly to the government.
translations.idiomatic: A timber market would resemble the horse market—benefiting the people without burdening the state.

sentences.zh: 利三。

translations.literal: Benefit three.
translations.idiomatic: Third benefit.

sentences.zh: 大舉之害酷而希，零竊之害輕而數。

translations.literal: The harm of great campaigns is cruel but rare; the harm of petty theft is light but frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Major raids are devastating but rare; petty raids are lighter but constant.

sentences.zh: 小歹青不掠錦、義，零竊少矣。

translations.literal: If Xiaodaqing does not raid Jin and Yi, petty thefts will be fewer.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaodaqing refrains from raiding Jinzhou and Yizhou, petty raids will diminish.

sentences.zh: 又西不助長昂，東不助炒花，則敵勢漸分。

translations.literal: Moreover, if westward he does not aid Changang and eastward he does not aid Chaohua, then enemy strength will gradually divide.
translations.idiomatic: If he ceases aiding Changang in the west and Chaohua in the east, enemy strength will divide.

sentences.zh: 即寧前、廣寧患亦漸減。

translations.literal: Then troubles at Ningqian and Guangning will also gradually lessen.
translations.idiomatic: Troubles at Ningqian and Guangning will also ease.

sentences.zh: 且大舉先報，又得預為備。

translations.literal: Moreover, great campaigns are reported in advance, and we can also prepare beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Major campaigns are announced in advance, giving time to prepare.

sentences.zh: 利四。

translations.literal: Benefit four.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth benefit.

sentences.zh: 零竊既希，邊人益得修備。

translations.literal: Once petty theft is rare, border people can all the more repair defenses.
translations.idiomatic: With fewer petty raids, border people can better restore their defenses.

sentences.zh: 利五。

translations.literal: Benefit five.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth benefit.

sentences.zh: 疏入，從之。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 化龍尋以病去，木市亦停止。

translations.literal: Hualong soon left on account of illness, and the timber market was also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong soon resigned on account of illness, and the timber market was suspended.

sentences.zh: 其後總兵官馬林復議開市，與巡撫李植相左，論久不決，小歹青遂復為寇雲。

translations.literal: Afterward the commander-in-chief Ma Lin again proposed opening the market; he clashed with Grand Coordinator Li Zhi, discussion long went undecided, and Xiaodaqing then again became a raider—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Commander Ma Lin again proposed reopening the market, clashed with Grand Coordinator Li Zhi, and debate dragged on until Xiaodaqing resumed raiding.

sentences.zh: 二十七年三月，化龍起故官，總督湖廣、川、貴軍務兼巡撫四川，討播州叛臣楊應龍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-seventh year Hualong was raised from his former office, made supreme commander of military affairs in Huguang, Sichuan, and Guizhou and concurrently grand coordinator of Sichuan, to attack the Bozhou rebel subject Yang Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 27 (1599) Hualong was recalled to serve as supreme commander of Huguang, Sichuan, and Guizhou and grand coordinator of Sichuan to suppress the Bozhou rebel Yang Yinglong.

sentences.zh: 應龍之先曰楊鏗。

translations.literal: Yinglong's ancestor was Yang Keng.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong's ancestor was Yang Keng.

sentences.zh: 明初內附，授宣慰使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming he submitted inward and was appointed pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming times the family submitted and received the title of pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 應龍性猜狠嗜殺。

translations.literal: Yinglong by nature was suspicious, fierce, and addicted to killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong was suspicious, brutal, and bloodthirsty by nature.

sentences.zh: 數從征調，恃功驕蹇。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns and summons, relying on merit to be proud and obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Having joined repeated campaigns, he grew arrogant on his merits.

sentences.zh: 知川兵脆弱，陰有據蜀誌，間出剽州縣。

translations.literal: Knowing Sichuan troops were weak, he secretly harbored the ambition to hold Shu and from time to time went out to plunder prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Sichuan troops were weak, he secretly aimed to seize the province and raided outlying districts.

sentences.zh: 嬖小妻田雌鳳，讒殺妻張氏，屠其家。

translations.literal: He favored a young wife Tian Cifeng, slandered and killed his wife Lady Zhang, and slaughtered her family.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring a concubine, Tian Cifeng, he slandered and killed his principal wife Lady Zhang and massacred her family.

sentences.zh: 用誅罰立威，所屬五司七姓不堪其虐，走貴州告變。

translations.literal: He used executions and punishments to establish awe; the five commissions and seven clans under him could not bear his cruelty and fled to Guizhou to report the disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled by terror; the five commissions and seven clans under him, unable to endure his cruelty, fled to Guizhou to report rebellion.

sentences.zh: 巡撫葉夢熊疏請大征。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ye Mengxiong memorialized requesting a major campaign.
