translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ye Mengxiong memorialized for a major expedition.

sentences.zh: 詔不聽，逮系重慶獄。

translations.literal: An edict did not listen; he was arrested and imprisoned in Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused; he was arrested and imprisoned in Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 應龍詭將兵征倭自效，得脫歸。

translations.literal: Yinglong falsely offered to lead troops against the Japanese wokou to prove loyalty and obtained release to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong falsely offered troops against the wokou, secured release, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 復逮，不出。

translations.literal: He was arrested again and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Arrested again, he refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 四川巡撫王繼光發兵討，覆於白石，應龍諉罪諸苗。

translations.literal: Sichuan Grand Coordinator Wang Jiguang sent troops to attack; they were destroyed at Baishi; Yinglong shifted blame to the various Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Grand Coordinator Wang Jiguang attacked but was destroyed at Baishi; Yinglong blamed the Miao tribes.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命邢玠總督。

translations.literal: The court appointed Xing Jie supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Xing Jie supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 值東西用兵，勢未能窮治，因招撫之。

translations.literal: It happened that troops were engaged east and west; the situation could not thoroughly punish him, and therefore he was won over by pacification.
translations.idiomatic: With wars raging east and west, the court could not pursue him to the end and pacified him instead.

sentences.zh: 應龍益結生苗，奪五司七姓地，並湖廣四十八屯以畀之，歲出侵掠。

translations.literal: Yinglong increasingly joined with the raw Miao, seized the lands of the five commissions and seven clans, and together with forty-eight tun of Huguang granted them to the Miao; each year he went out to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong rallied the unassimilated Miao, seized the lands of the five commissions and seven clans, and granted them Huguang's forty-eight military colonies, raiding yearly.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，敗官軍於飛練堡，都司楊國柱、指揮李廷棟等皆死。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year he defeated government troops at Feilian Fort; Regional Commander Yang Guozhu, Commander Li Tingdong, and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: That February he routed government forces at Feilian Fort; Regional Commander Yang Guozhu, Commander Li Tingdong, and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 已，復破殺綦江參將房嘉寵、遊擊張良賢，投屍蔽江下。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he again defeated and killed Qijiang Assistant Commander Fang Jiachong and Mobile Corps Commander Zhang Liangxian, casting corpses to cover the river downstream.
translations.idiomatic: He then destroyed Qijiang Assistant Commander Fang Jiachong and Mobile Corps Commander Zhang Liangxian and cast their bodies into the river until it was choked with corpses.

sentences.zh: 偽軍師孫時泰請直取重慶，搗成都，劫蜀王為質，而應龍遷延，聲言爭地界，冀曲赦如曩時。

translations.literal: The false military adviser Sun Shitai requested to strike straight for Chongqing, raid Chengdu, and seize the Prince of Shu as hostage; but Yinglong delayed, claiming to dispute boundaries, hoping for lenient pardon as in former times.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Sun Shitai urged a direct strike on Chongqing and Chengdu and seizing the Prince of Shu as hostage, but Yinglong delayed, claiming a boundary dispute and hoping for leniency as before.

sentences.zh: 化龍至成都，征兵未至，亦謬為好語縻之。

translations.literal: Hualong reached Chengdu; levied troops had not arrived; he also falsely spoke kind words to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong reached Chengdu before reinforcements arrived and also strung Yinglong along with conciliatory words.

sentences.zh: 帝聞綦江破，大怒。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the Qijiang defeat, he was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the Qijiang disaster, the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 追褫前四川、貴州巡撫譚希思、江東之職，而賜化龍劍，假便宜討賊。

translations.literal: He retroactively stripped former Sichuan and Guizhou grand coordinators Tan Xisi and Jiang Dongzhi of office, bestowed a sword on Hualong, and granted discretionary power to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped former Sichuan and Guizhou grand coordinators Tan Xisi and Jiang Dongzhi of rank, gave Hualong the imperial sword, and granted discretionary authority to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊焚東坡、爛橋，梗湖、貴路，又焚龍泉，走都司楊惟忠。

translations.literal: The bandits burned Dongpo and Lanqiao, blocked the Huguang and Guizhou routes, also burned Longquan, and drove off Regional Commander Yang Weizhong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels burned Dongpo and Lanqiao, blocked routes to Huguang and Guizhou, burned Longquan, and drove off Regional Commander Yang Weizhong.

sentences.zh: 化龍劾諸大帥不用命者，沈尚文逮治，童元鎮、劉廷皆革職充為事官。

translations.literal: Hualong impeached the great commanders who did not obey orders; Shen Shangwen was arrested and punished; Tong Yuanzhen and Liu Ting were all stripped of office and made officers on probation.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong impeached disobedient commanders; Shen Shangwen was arrested, and Tong Yuanzhen and Liu Ting were reduced to probationary officers.

sentences.zh: 諸軍大集，化龍先檄水西兵三萬守貴州，斷招苗路，乃移重慶，大誓文武。

translations.literal: The armies gathered in force; Hualong first ordered thirty thousand Shuixi troops to guard Guizhou and cut the route for recruiting Miao, then moved to Chongqing and swore in civil and military officials on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: As armies massed, Hualong first posted thirty thousand Shuixi troops in Guizhou to block Miao recruitment routes, then moved to Chongqing and administered a grand oath to civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，分八道進兵。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, troops advanced in eight routes.
translations.idiomatic: The following February he launched eight columns.

sentences.zh: 川師四路：總兵官劉綎由綦江，總兵官馬孔英由南川，總兵官吳廣由合江，副將曹希彬受廣節制，由永寧。

translations.literal: Sichuan forces in four routes: Commander Liu Ting by Qijiang, Commander Ma Kongying by Nanchuan, Commander Wu Guang by Hejiang, Vice General Cao Xibin under Guang's command by Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Four Sichuan columns: Commander Liu Ting via Qijiang, Ma Kongying via Nanchuan, Wu Guang via Hejiang, and Cao Xibin under Wu Guang via Yongning.

sentences.zh: 黔師三路：總兵官童元鎮由烏江，參將朱鶴齡受元鎮節制，統宣慰使安疆臣由沙溪，總兵官李應祥由興隆。

translations.literal: Guizhou forces in three routes: Commander Tong Yuanzhen by Wujiang, Assistant Commander Zhu Heling under Yuanzhen's command, Pacification Commissioner An Jiangchen commanding by Shaxi, Commander Li Yingxiang by Xinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Three Guizhou columns: Tong Yuanzhen via the Wujiang, Zhu Heling under him, Pacification Commissioner An Jiangchen via Shaxi, and Li Yingxiang via Xinglong.

sentences.zh: 楚師一路分兩翼：總兵官陳璘由偏橋，副總兵陳良比受璘節制，由龍泉。

translations.literal: Huguang forces in one route divided in two wings: Commander Chen Lin by Pianqiao, Vice Commander Chen Liangbi under Lin's command by Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: One Huguang column in two wings: Chen Lin via Pianqiao and Chen Liangbi via Longquan under his command.

sentences.zh: 每路兵三萬，官兵三之，土司七之。

translations.literal: Each route had thirty thousand troops: government soldiers three parts, native chieftains seven parts.
translations.idiomatic: Each column numbered thirty thousand men, three-tenths regular troops and seven-tenths native levies.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫郭子章駐貴陽，湖廣巡撫支可大移沅州，化龍自將中軍策應。

translations.literal: Guizhou Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang garrisoned Guiyang; Huguang Grand Coordinator Zhi Kedai moved to Yuanzhou; Hualong himself led the central army in support.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang held Guiyang, Huguang Grand Coordinator Zhi Kedai moved to Yuanzhou, and Hualong commanded the central reserve.

sentences.zh: 帝以楚地遼闊，又擢江鐸為僉都御史，巡撫偏、沅。

translations.literal: Because Huguang territory was vast, the emperor also promoted Jiang Duo to assistant censor-in-chief and made him grand coordinator of Pian and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huguang was vast, the emperor also promoted Jiang Duo to assistant censor-in-chief as grand coordinator of Pianqiao and Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 湖廣設偏沅巡撫，自鐸始也。

translations.literal: Huguang established the Pian-Yuan grand coordinator—from Duo it began.
translations.idiomatic: The Pian-Yuan grand coordinator post in Huguang began with Jiang Duo.

sentences.zh: 推官高折枝先以南川兵進，據桑木鎮，綎復自綦江入。

translations.literal: Magistrate-adjunct Gao Zhezhi first advanced with Nanchuan troops, seized Sangmu Town; Ting again entered from Qijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate-adjunct Gao Zhezhi advanced first from Nanchuan and seized Sangmu Town, and Liu Ting entered again from Qijiang.

sentences.zh: 應龍以勁兵二萬屬其子朝棟曰：「爾破綦江，馳南川，盡焚積聚，彼無能為也。」

translations.literal: Yinglong entrusted twenty thousand picked troops to his son Chaodong, saying: You broke Qijiang—dash to Nanchuan, burn all stores, and they can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong gave his son Chaodong twenty thousand elite troops, saying: "You destroyed Qijiang—rush to Nanchuan, burn all their stores, and they can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 比抗諸路兵，皆大敗，應龍頓足嘆曰：「吾不用時泰計，今死矣！」

translations.literal: When he resisted the troops of the various routes, all were greatly defeated; Yinglong stamped his feet and sighed, saying: I did not use Shitai's plan—now I am dead!
translations.idiomatic: But when he met the columns he was routed everywhere; Yinglong stamped his feet and cried: "I did not heed Shitai's plan—now I am finished!"

sentences.zh: 或言水西佐賊，化龍詰之疆臣，斬賊使，二氏交遂絕。

translations.literal: Some said Shuixi aided the bandits; Hualong questioned Jiangchen, beheaded the bandit envoy, and ties between the two houses were thus severed.
translations.idiomatic: When rumor said Shuixi was aiding the rebels, Hualong confronted An Jiangchen, executed the rebel envoy, and the alliance between the two houses was broken.

sentences.zh: 烏江兵敗績，逮下元鎮於理，諸將益奮。

translations.literal: The Wujiang troops suffered defeat; Yuanzhen was arrested and brought to justice; the generals were increasingly spirited.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat on the Wujiang, Tong Yuanzhen was arrested, and the other generals fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 綎先入婁山關，直抵海龍囤，璘、疆臣兵亦至。

translations.literal: Ting first entered Loushan Pass and went straight to Hailong Stockade; Lin's and Jiangchen's troops also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ting entered Loushan Pass first and reached Hailong Stockade, followed by Chen Lin and An Jiangchen.

sentences.zh: 賊勢急，上囤死守，遣使詐降。

translations.literal: The bandits' situation was desperate; they held the upper stockade to the death and sent envoys in false surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, the rebels held the upper stockade and sent envoys feigning surrender.

sentences.zh: 化龍檄諸將斬使，焚書。

translations.literal: Hualong ordered the generals by dispatch to behead the envoys and burn the letters.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong ordered the generals to execute the envoys and burn their letters.

sentences.zh: 以綎與應龍有舊，諭無通賊，綎械其人以自明。

translations.literal: Because Ting had old ties with Yinglong, he was instructed not to communicate with the bandits; Ting shackled the man to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Ting had old ties with Yinglong, Hualong warned him against collusion; Ting shackled the messenger to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 八路兵皆會囤下，築長圍困之，更番叠攻。

translations.literal: The eight-route armies all gathered below the stockade, built a long encirclement to besiege it, and attacked in rotating waves.
translations.idiomatic: All eight columns converged below the stockade, built a long encirclement, and attacked in relays.

sentences.zh: 六月，綎破土、月二城，應龍窘，與二妾俱縊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Ting breached the Tu and Yue secondary forts; Yinglong was cornered and hanged himself together with two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Ting breached the Tu and Yue forts; cornered, Yinglong hanged himself with two concubines.

sentences.zh: 明晨，官軍入城，七子皆被執。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day government troops entered the city; seven sons were all seized.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day government troops entered the citadel and seized all seven sons.

sentences.zh: 詔磔應龍屍並子朝棟於市。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yinglong's corpse and his son Chaodong dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yinglong's corpse and his son Chaodong dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 自出師至滅賊，凡百有十四日。

translations.literal: From dispatching the army to destroying the bandits, in all one hundred fourteen days.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening of the campaign to the destruction of the rebels took only one hundred fourteen days.

sentences.zh: 播自唐乾符中入楊氏，二十九世，八百余年，至應龍而絕，以其地置遵義、平越二府，分屬川、貴。

translations.literal: Bozhou since the Qianfu era of Tang entered the Yang house, twenty-nine generations, more than eight hundred years; at Yinglong it ended; with its territory were established the two prefectures Zunyi and Pingyue, divided between Sichuan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou had been held by the Yang clan since Tang Qianfu (874–879), through twenty-nine generations and more than eight hundred years, until Yinglong's line ended; its territory was reorganized as the prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue, divided between Sichuan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 化龍初聞父喪，以金革起復，至是乞歸終制。

translations.literal: When Hualong first heard of his father's death, he was recalled from mourning on account of military affairs; at this point he requested to return and complete the full mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong had been recalled from mourning for his father on military grounds; he now asked to return home and complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 三十一年四月，起工部右侍郎，總理河道，與淮、揚巡撫李三才奏開淤河，由直河入泇口抵夏鎮二百六十里，避黃河呂梁之險。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-first year he was raised to right vice minister of the Ministry of Works to oversee river works; with the Huai and Yang grand coordinator Li Sancai he memorialized to open the silted river, from the straight channel entering the Si mouth to Xia Town two hundred sixty li, avoiding the peril of the Yellow River at Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 31 (1603) he was appointed right vice minister of Works to oversee the Grand Canal and, with Huai-Yang Grand Coordinator Li Sancai, memorialized to dredge a silted channel two hundred sixty li from the straight river through the Si estuary to Xia Town, bypassing the hazard of the Yellow River at Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 再以憂去，未代。

translations.literal: He again left on account of mourning and was not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned again for mourning and was not replaced.

sentences.zh: 敘前平播功，晉兵部尚書，加少保，蔭一子世錦衣指揮使。

translations.literal: When recounting his earlier merit in pacifying Bozhou, he was advanced to minister of the Ministry of War, made junior guardian, and one son was granted hereditary commandant of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Bozhou he was promoted to minister of War and junior guardian, and one son received a hereditary post as commandant of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 三十五年夏，起戎政尚書。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-fifth year he was raised to minister of military administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 35 (1607) he was appointed minister of military administration.

sentences.zh: 化龍以京營根本，奏陳十一濫、十二苦、十九宜，又上屯政十二事，皆置不理。

translations.literal: Hualong, because the capital garrisons were fundamental, memorialized setting forth eleven abuses, twelve hardships, and nineteen measures that should be taken, and also submitted twelve items on garrison-farmland policy—all were set aside without handling.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the capital garrisons fundamental to defense, Hualong memorialized eleven abuses, twelve hardships, and nineteen reforms, and twelve proposals on garrison farmland—all were ignored.

sentences.zh: 兵部自二十七年後，左、右侍郎皆空署。

translations.literal: Since the twenty-seventh year the left and right vice ministers of the Ministry of War had all been vacant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Since year 27 the left and right vice ministers of War had gone unfilled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，尚書蕭大亨亦致仕，化龍掌部事。

translations.literal: Before long Minister Xiao Daheng also retired; Hualong took charge of ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Minister Xiao Daheng retired as well, and Hualong took charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 三十七年正月，京師訛言寇至，民爭避匿，邊民逃入都門者亦數萬，九門晝閉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-seventh year, rumor in the capital said raiders had arrived; the people vied to flee and hide; border people who fled into the capital gates also numbered tens of thousands; the nine gates were closed by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 37 (1609) rumor spread in the capital that raiders were coming; crowds fled in panic, tens of thousands of frontier refugees poured through the gates, and the nine city gates were closed by day.

sentences.zh: 輔臣言兵部尚書惟一人，何以應猝變，帝亦不報。

translations.literal: A chief minister said the minister of War was only one man—how could he meet sudden change? The emperor also did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister asked how a single minister of War could meet sudden crisis; the emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 遼戰士二萬余皆老弱，而稅監高淮肆虐，遼人切齒。

translations.literal: More than twenty thousand Liaodong fighting men were all old and weak, while the tax supervisor Gao Huai ran rampant; Liaodong people gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong's twenty thousand-odd fighting men were old and weak, while tax supervisor Gao Huai ran rampant, leaving the people bitter with rage.

sentences.zh: 化龍請停稅課，且增兵萬人，又條上兵食款戰之策，帝皆不報。

translations.literal: Hualong requested stopping tax levies and also increasing troops by ten thousand; he also itemized policies on troops, provisions, appeasement, and warfare—the emperor replied to none.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong asked to halt tax levies, add ten thousand troops, and submitted detailed plans on manpower, supplies, appeasement, and war—the emperor answered none of them.

sentences.zh: 一品秩滿，加柱國、少傅兼太子太保。

translations.literal: When his first-rank term was complete, he was made pillar of state, junior mentor, and concurrent grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his first-rank term expired he was made pillar of state, junior mentor, and grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年七十。

translations.literal: He died in office at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 謚襄毅，贈少師，加贈太師。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Xiangyi; granted junior mentor; further granted grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Xiangyi, granted junior mentor, and later grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 化龍具文武才。

translations.literal: Hualong possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Hualong possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 播州之役，以劉綎驕蹇，先摧挫之而薦其才，故綎為盡力。

translations.literal: In the Bozhou campaign, because Liu Ting was proud and obstinate, he first humbled him and then recommended his talent; therefore Ting exerted himself fully.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bozhou campaign, finding Liu Ting proud and difficult, he first humbled him and then praised his ability, and Liu Ting served with full devotion.

sentences.zh: 開河之功，為漕渠永利，詳見《河渠志》。

translations.literal: The merit of opening the river brought lasting benefit to the transport channel; details are fully seen in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: His canal work brought lasting benefit to the transport system; see the Treatise on Rivers and Canals for details.

sentences.zh: 江鐸，字士振，仁和人。

translations.literal: Jiang Duo, style Shizhen, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Duo, whose style was Shizhen, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 高祖比，景泰時為禮科給事中。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bi, in the Jingtai reign was a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bi served as a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites under the Jingtai emperor.

sentences.zh: 劾石亨怙寵罔上，有直聲。

translations.literal: He impeached Shi Heng for relying on favor and deceiving the sovereign, and had a reputation for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Shi Heng for abusing imperial favor and won a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 官至山東參政。

translations.literal: His office reached Shandong administrative vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrative vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瀾，正德時南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lan was minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Rites in the Zhengde reign.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lan was minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Rites under the Zhengde emperor.

sentences.zh: 卒謚文昭。

translations.literal: On death he was given the posthumous title Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖曉，嘉靖中工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiao was vice minister of the Ministry of Works in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiao was vice minister of Works in the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 父圻，萬歷初廣西提學僉事。

translations.literal: His father Qi was educational intendant of Guangxi at the beginning of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi was educational intendant of Guangxi early in the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 父母疾，嘗藥舐糞。

translations.literal: When his parents were ill, he tasted their medicine and licked their stool.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents fell ill he tasted their medicine and even tasted their stool—a supreme act of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 居喪寢苫三年，經寢室必俯其首，妻經夫廬亦然。

translations.literal: In mourning he dwelt on the rush mat three years; passing the mourning hut he always bowed his head, and his wife passing her husband's hut did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned on a rush mat for three years, always bowing his head when passing the mourning hut; his wife did the same.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人私謚為孝端先生。

translations.literal: On death his students privately gave him the posthumous title Master Xiaoduan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his students privately gave him the title Master Xiaoduan.

sentences.zh: 自比至鐸五世皆進士。

translations.literal: From Bi to Duo for five generations all were jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: From Bi down to Duo, five generations produced jinshi.

sentences.zh: 而曉弟暉，正德中為庶吉士，與舒芬等諫南巡受杖。

translations.literal: Xiao's younger brother Hui, in the Zhengde reign was a Hanlin bachelor; with Shu Fen and others he remonstrated against the southern tour and was beaten with rods.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao's younger brother Hui, a Hanlin bachelor under Zhengde, joined Shu Fen and others in opposing the southern tour and was beaten with rods.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，由編修出為河南僉事。

translations.literal: In the Shizong reign, from compiler he went out as Henan administrative vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiajing emperor he left the Hanlin Academy to serve as administrative vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 鐸登第在萬歷二年。

translations.literal: Duo passed the examination in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Duo passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 2 (1574).

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 累官山西按察使，擢撫偏、沅。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became Shanxi surveillance commissioner and was promoted to grand coordinator of Pian and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and was promoted to grand coordinator of Pianqiao and Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夾攻楊應龍有功，與郭子章皆蔭一子世錦衣指揮。

translations.literal: In the converging attack on Yang Yinglong he had merit; he and Guo Zizhang were each granted one son hereditary commandant of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He earned merit in the converging attack on Yang Yinglong; he and Guo Zizhang each received a hereditary commandant's post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard for a son.

sentences.zh: 丁母艱去。

translations.literal: He left on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 奪情，命留討皮林諸洞蠻，平之。

translations.literal: His mourning was shortened; he was ordered to remain and attack the various cave Miao of Pilin; he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was ordered to suppress the Miao of the Pilin caves and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 詳具《陳璘傳》。

translations.literal: Details are fully set forth in the biography of Chen Lin.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Chen Lin for full details.

sentences.zh: 以勞疾歸。

translations.literal: He returned on account of toil and illness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home worn out by illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: On death he was granted right vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：哱拜一降人耳，雖假以爵秩，而憑藉未厚。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Piba was only a surrendered man; although enfeoffed with rank and title, his backing was not thick.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Piba was only a surrendered tribesman; though granted rank and title, his base of support was thin.

sentences.zh: 倉猝發難，據鎮城，聯外寇，邊鄙為之騷然，武備之弛，有由來矣。

translations.literal: Suddenly launching trouble, seizing the garrison town, linking with outside raiders—the border regions were thrown into turmoil for it; the slackening of military preparedness had long-standing causes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he rose suddenly, seized the garrison city, and allied with outside raiders, throwing the frontier into turmoil—a sign of how long military preparedness had been neglected.

sentences.zh: 楊應龍惡稔貫盈，自速殄滅。

translations.literal: Yang Yinglong's evil was ripe and full; he hastened his own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yinglong's crimes were ripe and full, and he hastened his own destruction.

sentences.zh: 然盤踞積久，地形險惡，非師武臣力，奏績豈易言哉！

translations.literal: Yet he had entrenched himself for long accumulation; the terrain was perilous and harsh—without martial generals' force, reporting achievement would not be easy to speak of!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had entrenched himself for years in rugged terrain; without able generals, victory could hardly have been reported so easily!

sentences.zh: 李化龍之功可與韓雍、項忠相埒，較寧夏之役，難易懸殊矣。

translations.literal: Li Hualong's achievement can be ranked with Han Yong and Xiang Zhong; compared with the Ningxia campaign, the difficulty and ease are vastly different.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hualong's achievement ranks with those of Han Yong and Xiang Zhong—a feat of an altogether different order of difficulty from the Ningxia campaign.
